correctness.rationale: The exact cone geodesic law and independent area sampling yield the radial and angular moment formulas. Explicit sign factorizations and elementary rigorous bounds on pi and square roots establish all strictly alternating endpoint inequalities. Continuity yields three distinct roots in disjoint intervals for each of two observables; positive scaling fixes the desired absolute moment or area. Direct numerical integration tests the original distance integral. No numerical roots are relied upon to establish an infinite existence theorem.

value.rationale: The natural two-parameter singular flat cone family has two practically meaningful two-number intrinsic measurement signatures. The theorem shows robust at-least-threefold nonidentifiability on nonempty open signature regions in both the fixed-area and two-moment inverse settings, with exact analytic witnesses and geometry-driven interval endpoints. It is a motivated counterexample to parameter reconstruction, not a random low-order scalar calculation.
